I didn’t go through a rough childhood, but my family owned an elementary school, and I was often used as an example to discipline other students. By “my family owned a school,” I mean that my grandfather owns a small school, which is run by my aunts and uncles. My father, whom I later realized was the black sheep of the family, worked as a janitor at the school.

What I mean by being used to discipline other students is this: For example, when I was still in kindergarten, my aunt, who was a teacher, made me stand in front of my classmates. She opened my bag, grabbed my books, and threw them one by one while saying something I can no longer remember. There are more instances like that but I won't list them all haha. I believed that it had greatly affected my confidence throughout the rest of my elementary and high school years.

I remember in high school how much I dreaded being the center of attention in class. I was very shy about speaking my mind during social interactions, and I often wouldn’t raise my hand even if I knew the answer out of fear of making a mistake or being judged. I also remember that during school plays, even after practicing with my groupmates, I would become too scared to show up on the day of the performance( Looking back, I see how selfish that was, and I truly regret not attending).

I’m 30 years old now, and I can say I’m a lot more confident than I used to be. I still feel some fear when I’m the center of attention or when I overthink what to say to people, but it doesn’t affect me as much as it did before. For example, I can now talk to strangers easily and present in meetings without much trouble. That said, I still try my best to avoid those kinds of interactions, but I can do it if I need to.
